title: Flexible micro-lease transient reservoirs: fine-grained short-term reserved slots for bursty tenants
creator: Ava Martinez
problem_statement: Customers with variable traffic patterns want guaranteed burst capacity for short windows (minutes to a few hours) without committing to long-term reserved slots. Current reserved pools are coarse-grained (daily/weekly) and either over-provision or risk SLA misses during spikes. We need a mechanism that lets tenants acquire short-lived, billable micro-leases that prewarm and optionally preempt best-effort work, while preserving fairness and predictable tail latency for other reserved tenants.
background: Redwood Dedicated offers long-lived reserved pools and opportunistic burst capacity. Multiple PM PRDs address large-scale reservation policies and fairshare, but none provide a first-class, atomic short-term reservation primitive optimized for sudden spikes. Customers ask for an API/console control to request guaranteed capacity for a defined time-scope (e.g., 10 minutes, 2 hours), with clear accounting and eviction guarantees. This PRD defines the feature set, UX, API, orchestration semantics, and acceptance criteria for "micro-lease" transient reservoirs.
goals: Provide an API and Console control allowing tenants to request short-lived reserved capacity (micro-lease) with explicit duration and optional prewarm behavior
Ensure micro-leases can be satisfied with predictable tail latency (p99/p999) for allocated requests within the lease window
Expose clear billing/credits and metrics for micro-lease usage and success rate
Enforce fair eviction and spillback semantics so micro-leases do not destabilize long-lived reservations or degrade cluster SLOs
non_goals: Replace long-term reserved commitments or pricing models
Support arbitrarily large instant capacity spikes without integration with global autoscale policies
Provide strong multi-region replication for micro-lease state in the initial rollout (single-zone semantics acceptable for MVP)
user_stories: As an app owner, I want to request a 30-minute 2-GPU micro-lease before a product launch email blast so my requests get guaranteed throughput
As an SRE, I want levers to limit total concurrent micro-leases per tenant and per-zone to avoid noisy neighbor pathologies
As an engineering manager, I want a billing ledger and audit trail showing when micro-leases were granted, used, and evicted
requirements: API: POST /v1/dedicated/microleases -> request parameters: tenant_id, num_gpus, duration_minutes, prewarm:true|false, max_latency_ms (optional)
Console: one-click 'Create micro-lease' modal with duration presets and a cost estimate
Orchestration: allocate nodes/slots and optionally prewarm model caches and KV caches for leases that request prewarm
Admission: if micro-lease cannot be satisfied within X seconds, return a clear quota/failure reason and offer backfill options
Billing: micro-lease consumption must appear as a line-item in tenant billing with start/end timestamps and usage tokens consumed
Isolation: micro-lease must be able to preempt best-effort/shared capacity according to a configured priority matrix but not soft-evict other active micro-leases with higher priority
Eviction: eviction policy must follow an explicit ordered rule-set (oldest-best-effort -> lowest-priority-microlease) and provide 30s grace for in-flight requests when feasible
Telemetry: emit metrics for lease_request_rate, lease_grant_rate, lease_eviction_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency for requests served under micro-lease, and cost_delta compared to baseline
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end API flow: create, activate, query, and expire a micro-lease in staging; responses conform to schema and lifecycle states
Tail latency: for a synthetic tenant workload using micro-lease, p99 generation latency must meet the configured max_latency_ms or be within 20% of long-lived reserved pool baseline

Fairness: under contention test with 50 tenants requesting overlapping micro-leases, eviction order follows policy and no tenant experiences >20% extra 99th percentile latency compared to baseline for >15 minutes
Prewarm effectiveness: prewarm=true must reduce cold-start latencies for target model by at least 40% vs no-prewarm for the first 500 requests post-allocation in lab tests
Billing traceability: billing shows accurate timestamps and token counts for 95%+ of micro-lease activations in a 24-hour test window
Operational safety: feature toggled by org-level flag; can be disabled without leaving orphaned allocations in the cluster
design_considerations: Micro-lease state machine should be minimal: REQUESTED -> PENDING (resources being allocated/prewarm) -> ACTIVE (lease window) -> EXPIRED/EVicted. We must avoid hypertight coupling between micro-lease controller and global autoscaler; controller should request capacity via existing allocation APIs and have configurable timeouts. Prewarm should use best-effort KV and prefix cache warming for the specified model/version. Lease requests should be throttled per-tenant and optionally attach to billing-allowance tokens to avoid denial-of-service via lease spam.
api_spec_notes: Request/response must be backward-compatible. Use X-Idempotency-Key for retries. Duration granularity = minutes; max allowed duration default = 180 minutes (configurable per-org). Failure codes must include 429 (quota), 409 (conflict), 503 (capacity) with structured reason strings. Lease lifecycle events must emit CloudEvents to the tenant's webhook endpoint if configured.
orchestration_and_runtime_notes: Allocation controller will try to satisfy micro-lease from: 1) spare slots in tenant's reserved pool 2) reserved soft headroom 3) shared opportunistic pool with preemption. If only shared pool used, label lease as 'best-effort-backed' and downgrade SLA accordingly. Prewarming sequence: attach container, load weights into memory, prefill KV cache with tenant-provided prefixes if available, warm tokenizers. Allow warmup healthcheck endpoint to report readiness for precise activation time.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit lease.created, lease.activated, lease.evicted, lease.expired events in telemetry stream
Alert: if eviction_rate > 5% sustained for 10m -> page capacity-oncall
Alert: if p99_under_lease increases >2x baseline for 15m -> page runtime performance owners
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated (org-level). Start with Redwood internal org and 3 early access tenants
Week 1: internal canary in staging with synthetic traffic; validate API and basic flows
Week 2: internal canary in production (low volume) for model-family A
Week 3: invite 3 EA customers; monitor metrics and iterate eviction heuristics
Gradual ramp to GA: unlock per-org flag via sales/CS readiness and billing integration
migration_plan: No migration needed for existing long-lived reservations. Provide a one-click console flow to convert short-term scheduled windows into micro-lease requests for customers who previously used ad-hoc scripts. Export historical usage as CSV for billing reconciliation during early rollout.
dependencies: Billing: line-item primitives and time-windowed ledger entries (billing team)
Runtime: prewarm hooks and warmup-healthcheck API (runtime/inference infra)
Autoscaler: ability to honor micro-lease priority in allocation decisioning (orchestrator/autoscaler)
Console: new modal and cost-estimate component (DX)
Telemetry: events pipeline for lease lifecycle (observability)
Security: org-level feature flag gating and audit logging (security/compliance)
timeline: MVP delivery target: 6 weeks (design + infra + API + console baseline). Extended rollout and billing integrations by week 12.
success_metrics: Micro-lease adoption: >20 customers request at least one micro-lease in first 90 days after GA
Burst hit-rate: 90% of micro-lease activations successfully satisfy requested capacity without fallback
Customer satisfaction: <2 support incidents per 100 micro-lease activations related to inaccurate billing or major performance regressions
Cost efficiency: average token cost delta for workloads under lease <= 1.2x compared to equivalent reserved pool
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Micro-leases exhaust shared capacity and degrade holdup SLOs -> Mitigation: global soft cap on concurrent micro-leases and admission controller returning 503 with clear guidance
Risk: Billing reconciliation bugs causing disputed invoices -> Mitigation: ship ledger export and require two independent signals (allocation start + activation event) before billing
Risk: Eviction storm under widespread demand -> Mitigation: staggered prewarm windows, jittered lease start times, and priority decay rule to avoid thundering herd
Risk: Feature abused by attackers to cause allocation churn -> Mitigation: per-org throttles, rate limits, and idempotency requirements
open_questions: Should micro-lease cost be flat rate per GPU-minute or dynamic per current spot price? (finance input required)
What default eviction grace should we provide for long-running in-flight requests during preemption? (30s proposed)
Do we allow cross-region micro-leases or limit to single-zone in MVP? (single-zone recommended)
engineering_notes: Implementation to be split into (1) API surface and validation (2) orchestration controller to request capacity and trigger prewarm hooks (3) billing ledger integration and event emission (4) console UX. Unit and integration tests must include contention scenarios. Add feature-flag gating on org_id and operational kill-switch. Keep micro-lease state minimal to facilitate fail-safe expirations.
qa_plan: Automated tests: lifecycle state transitions, idempotent create, eviction order under synthetic contention. Performance tests: p99 targets for small and medium models under 1- and 2-GPU leases. Manual QA: console creation flows, billing line-item verification, and webhook subscription validation. Run chaos test to validate system behavior when orchestrator loses connectivity during active lease.
notes_for_support: Support playbook: how to query lease state with API, how to refund/adjust billing for disputed activations, and how to toggle org feature flag. Provide sample curl commands and common troubleshooting checklist. Create a runbook for capacity-oncall for eviction storm scenarios.
